The upper end of public servants come from very specific social groups (harvard, yale, major urban centers) which do tend to correlate with IQ but there are plenty of very capable people outside of these very limited social groups. By the numbers you can find plenty of people with an IQ of 130 in rural Georgia. 130 being the basic minimum IQ for most intellectually intensive work, meaning that someone with an IQ of 130 is perfectly capable of being a doctor, lawyer, governmental official, etc. Very few jobs require IQs beyond 130 (cutting edge scientist, Ivy League professor, president). Beyond 130 IQ is still meaningful but the variance in abilities starts to grow. What I mean by that is generally speaking a person with an IQ of say 120 will be better at just about every intellectual task than say someone with an IQ of 100. Having the absolute smartest person does not guarantee the best results. To the extent that something is a governmental function we should balance intelligence against temperament and intellectual diversity.
